name: Alamo Church Phase 7 - base (C3.00, E. Houston St west)
frame: plan feet from the sheet (1" = 10'), not state plane

regions.name: Hardscape: pavers on setting bed over 6 in concrete sub-slab

spec.source: C1.20 civil site details; no geotech supplied

basis: Alamo Site Area 7 streetscape (Pape-Dawson 11078-73, issue for construction 08/28/2026), sheet C3.00 at 1" = 10'. The sheets carry no text layer; spot grades and contour labels were read by OCR.

Finish grade from the proposed spot elevations (gutter and pavement shots; top-of-curb shots left out); existing ground from the spots marked EX, which sit mostly at the match lines. Inside the limits the existing surface is interpolated between those, so cut and fill from grade change alone are approximate; the design ties to existing within a few tenths.
Limits = the magenta PHASE 7 PROJECT LIMITS line traced from the sheet: 1,258 SY. 993 cells inside the line had no surface and were dropped.

One hardscape area over the whole limits at 16 in below finish grade: pavers (about 2.5 in assumed, thickness is on the landscape plans), 1 to 2 in setting bed, the 6 in concrete sub-slab of C1.20 detail 12, and 6 in of aggregate base course under sub-slabs and sidewalks (Exhibit B, RFI clarifications; WPM proposal #4 carries 420 TN of base for 12,500 SF, which is 6 in). Subgrade below is moisture conditioned.

Scope check against WPM proposal #4 (West Phase 7, 9/22/2026, 100% DD): 12,500 SF of sub-slab paver area there against 12,321 SF traced inside the project limits here. Not in this model: 125 CY of planter excavation to 18 in (planters are on the landscape plans), the 260 CY spoils haul allowance for other trades, demolition of pavers, sub-slab, curb and 8,200 SF of sidewalk and flagstone, and the two construction entrances.
Exhibit B requires excavation in 4 in lifts with a smooth bucket under archaeological monitoring, fine grading to 0.10 ft, 97 percent compaction under paving, and hauling spoils not reused.
No strip: the existing surface is street and sidewalk pavement, so its removal is demolition, not topsoil. No shrink or swell (standing decision).
